requirements.note: Inset grouped list of all 160 with title, 'Category · time' subtitle and star rating, chevron; header shows 'All Recipes · 160 recipes'.

Filter is a system pull-down menu with All + all nine categories (checkmark on current); search matches titles and ingredients and combines with category (Desserts 28 → 9 with 'egg'); good empty state 'No Desserts recipes match …' with Show All Recipes.
Separate sort menu: Name A–Z, Time quickest, Rating highest; all verified; button label reflects current sort.
Detail shows category, time, rating, servings stepper, ingredients and numbered steps; stepper scales amounts with fractions (2 → 2¾ at 5→7).
Heart in nav bar toggles; Favorites tab lists them with system swipe-to-delete and a hint; helpful empty state with Browse Recipes button.

bugs: At the largest text size list-row titles break inside words ('Crea / my / Chick / en') because the rating column keeps its width beside the title.
tells: Steps are laid out like LabeledContent: number on the left, step text right-aligned in grey as if it were a value. Reads oddly and wraps awkwardly at large text.
Ingredient rows at the largest text size have almost no vertical padding and sit tight against the separators.
Detail screen has no large title or header for the recipe name, only the inline nav title. Category/Time/Rating are a plain settings-style form, so it looks more like a settings page than a recipe.
Scaled fractions are sometimes imprecise (1.4 shown as 1½).
A.scroll: Smooth native collection-view scrolling: no blank or popping rows when flung and flung back, large title collapses properly, rubber-bands at the top. Scroll position is kept on returning from a recipe (shifted by about 13pt).

requirements.note: Plain list with title, tinted category, clock + time, star + rating, chevron; '160 recipes' subtitle under the large title.

Horizontal chip bar with All + all nine categories, plus a Category submenu in the toolbar menu; search covers titles and ingredients and combines with the chip (Desserts + 'egg' → 9); 'No Results for …' empty state with Search All Categories.
Toolbar menu with Name/Time/Rating (with icons) and current-sort value; all verified; sort choice even persists across relaunch.
Header with category, large title and Time/Servings/Rating tiles; servings stepper scales ingredients with fractions (4 → 5⅓ at 6→8); steps in numbered circles.
Heart toggles; Favorites tab with 'N saved recipes' subtitle, swipe-to-remove and Edit button; friendly empty state with Browse Recipes that switches tabs.

bugs: On first launch list rows are 92pt tall with extra space above the title. After the first re-sort or filter they become 77pt, so the list visibly changes density.
Favorites empty state (heart, title, text, Browse Recipes button) is invisible to accessibility: the tree shows only an 'Empty list' table, so VoiceOver cannot read or reach it.
tells: Custom-drawn category chip bar instead of a system control or menu; it scrolls away while the search field stays pinned, and list content shows through behind the floating search field while scrolling.
The recipe title appears twice on the detail screen: as the inline nav title and as the large header at the same time.
Header 'Servings' tile keeps showing the base serving count while the stepper shows the scaled count.
Search placeholder does not grow with Dynamic Type at the largest size.
B.scroll: Smooth fling and return with no blank or popping rows; nav title collapses into a centred title/subtitle. Rows do change height between first load and later reloads, and position on returning from a recipe shifts by about 10pt.

why: Both meet every requirement. B's detail screen is richer and better laid out (stat tiles, numbered step badges, scaled amounts highlighted), its empty and no-result states are more helpful, and it reflows cleanly at the largest text size. A's list titles break inside words at that size, and its steps are right-aligned grey 'values'. B's flaws are smaller: a hand-drawn chip bar, a row-height jump after the first reload, and an empty state that VoiceOver can't read.
